short: The last of the Severan dynasty, whose murder by his own troops opened fifty years of military anarchy.
full:
Severus Alexander became emperor at thirteen on 13 March 222 CE after the Praetorian Guard killed his cousin, the notorious Elagabalus, and installed him instead. Actual authority for most of his reign rested with his mother, Julia Mamaea, and a council of senior senators, who steered a cautious, conservative course after Elagabalus's excesses.

The arrangement satisfied the Senate but not the army. A costly, indecisive war against the newly aggressive Sasanian Persian empire and a hurried, poorly funded campaign on the Rhine left the legions resentful of a young emperor still dominated by his mother. In March 235 CE, near Mainz, mutinous troops murdered both Severus Alexander and Julia Mamaea and raised the officer Maximinus Thrax in his place, ending the Severan dynasty and opening the military crisis that followed.
